Baker Street. The iconic London address at 221B Baker Street where Sherlock Holmes and Dr. Watson live in Arthur Conan Doyle's detective stories. The lodging itself becomes almost a character in the narratives: a refuge where Holmes conducts chemical experiments, broods over cases, and expounds on his methods while Watson narrates their adventures. The address has transcended its fictional origins to become one of literature's most recognizable addresses, symbolizing the detective's intellectual sanctuary and the domestic partnership between Holmes and Watson.

Baker Street is a real London street in the West End, a fact that adds verisimilitude to the fictional narratives and allows readers to imaginatively locate the detective's residence. Holmes and Watson take lodgings with their landlady, Mrs. Hudson. The flat becomes the setting for many of Holmes's most famous deductions. His sitting room is furnished with the accumulated evidence of his cases: chemical apparatus, scrapbooks, pipes, and the violin he plays when contemplating difficult problems.

Dr. Watson, narrating from 221B, uses the setting as the domestic frame for his tales. Many stories begin with Watson and Holmes at breakfast or in the sitting room, establishing the investigative partnership and the comfortable familiarity between them. This domestic routine becomes the stable center from which the extraordinary investigations launch. The lodging represents a peculiar kind of domesticity for the detective fiction form—221B is the home base from which investigations begin and to which the detectives return for rest and reflection, distinguishing Conan Doyle's detective stories from other works in the genre.

The address has become so embedded in popular culture that tourists visit the real Baker Street in London seeking the fictional address. A small museum celebrates Holmes and Watson's residence. The fact that the real Baker Street exists alongside its fictional double has created a unique phenomenon in literary geography: readers can walk the same streets their fictional heroes walked. This collision between real and fictional London has made 221B Baker Street inseparable from the detective's identity and from the Victorian London that Conan Doyle depicts with such vivid social texture. The address endures as one of fiction's most powerful examples of how a specific, imagined domestic space can capture readers' imagination across generations.
